goal: Stops the node from wrongly penalizing addresses on a network that is temporarily unreachable, e.g. marking IPv6 or Tor peers terrible just because IPv4 connections keep succeeding.
Benefits node operators with partial connectivity (IPv6 down, broken Tor proxy) by preserving otherwise-good peers in addrman.

stratospher raised a nonblocking concern about permanently-unreachable-network addresses lingering uselessly, which the author acknowledged as an accepted tradeoff rather than fixing (stratospher, mzumsande).

result.summary: This PR makes AddrMan's m_last_good timestamp per-network instead of a single global value, so that a successful connection on one network (e.g. IPv4) no longer causes failed-connection counting against addresses on a different, currently-unreachable network (e.g. IPv6 or Tor). It also changes the initial value from 1 to 0 so failures aren't counted before any successful connection on that network has occurred. A new test demonstrates the bug and the fix.
result.problem: Node operators who can reach some networks but not others (commonly IPv6, or a broken Tor proxy) were having addresses on the unreachable network incorrectly marked as failing and eventually 'Terrible', purely because connections on a different, working network succeeded. This wrongly evicts otherwise-good peers and reduces network/path diversity, which matters for privacy-sensitive transports like Tor and I2P.

open_concerns: stratospher noted that if a network stays permanently unreachable, its addresses may linger uselessly in addrman until they age out or connectivity is restored; author agreed this is an accepted tradeoff rather than something to fix now.
resolved_concerns: naiyoma independently reproduced the bug on master with logs and confirmed the PR's per-network tracking fixes it.
